name: Crowdfunding and Social Media Fundraising for Terrorist Financing
description: Online fundraising platforms, social media appeals and messaging channels can be used to solicit small donations across many jurisdictions for violent groups, often presenting as humanitarian or community causes. Detection combines campaign content intelligence with payment patterns across payment processors, banks and platforms.

sources.text: FATF, Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment Guidance (2019)

exposure.rationale: Online fundraising with many small donations via platforms and wallets.

indicators.name: Campaign narrative linked to extremist content or designated groups
indicators.canon: Campaign narrative linked to extremist content or designated groups
indicators.desc: Fundraising page, post or channel references violent groups, glorifies violence or is linked to accounts removed for extremism.
indicators.ctx: Fundraising page, post or channel references violent groups, glorifies violence or is linked to accounts removed for extremism.
indicators.fp: Political or religious speech, and news reporting, may reference the same topics lawfully.

indicators.name: Many small donations from geographically diverse donors to a single organiser
indicators.canon: Many small donations from geographically diverse donors to a single organiser
indicators.desc: Large numbers of low-value contributions from many countries into one recipient account that then withdraws promptly.
indicators.ctx: Large numbers of low-value contributions from many countries into one recipient account that then withdraws promptly.
indicators.fp: Viral humanitarian appeals and memorial funds show similar patterns.

indicators.name: Payout to account unrelated to organiser or declared beneficiary
indicators.canon: Payout to account not matching verified identity or declared beneficiary
indicators.desc: Payouts or disbursements are directed to bank accounts, cards or wallets that do not match the verified customer or declared beneficiary.
indicators.ctx: Funds are paid to third-party accounts, prepaid cards or wallets that do not match the organiser's verified identity.
indicators.fp: Campaigns for medical treatment are often paid to relatives or institutions.

indicators.name: Use of coded language, rapid channel migration or deleted campaigns
indicators.canon: Use of coded language, rapid channel migration or deleted campaigns
indicators.desc: Organiser moves between platforms or handles, closes campaigns and restarts under new names after scrutiny.
indicators.ctx: Organiser moves between platforms or handles, closes campaigns and restarts under new names after scrutiny.
indicators.fp: Privacy-conscious users and harassment victims also change handles.

indicators.name: Donations routed to cryptocurrency addresses or messaging-app collection points
indicators.canon: Donations routed to cryptocurrency addresses or messaging-app collection points
indicators.desc: Appeal asks for crypto transfers or direct contact on encrypted channels instead of regulated payment methods.
indicators.ctx: Appeal asks for crypto transfers or direct contact on encrypted channels instead of regulated payment methods.
indicators.fp: Crypto donations are legitimate in some communities.

indicators.name: Campaigns exploiting a crisis event with unverified beneficiaries
indicators.canon: Campaigns exploiting a crisis event with unverified beneficiaries
indicators.desc: Appeals created immediately after conflict or disaster events with no known organisation behind them and no verifiable delivery route.
indicators.ctx: Appeals created immediately after conflict or disaster events with no known organisation behind them and no verifiable delivery route.
indicators.fp: Genuine rapid-response efforts frequently emerge informally.

indicators.name: Funds withdrawn as cash or via ATM in higher-risk border regions
indicators.canon: Cash or card use in border and transit areas near conflict zones
indicators.desc: Cash withdrawals, ATM or card use occur at transit points or border regions near conflict zones.
indicators.ctx: Collected funds are cashed out near conflict zones or high-risk borders shortly after payout.
indicators.fp: Residents and aid workers also transact in those regions.

indicators.name: Organiser account shows identity inconsistencies
indicators.canon: Inconsistent or synthetic identity data at onboarding
indicators.desc: Identity documents, contact details, geolocation or device data do not align, suggesting fabricated, stolen or misrepresented identity.
indicators.ctx: Organiser identity documents, contact details or IP geolocation do not align with claimed location or purpose.
indicators.fp: VPN use and travel create geolocation mismatches.
